company.name: Northrop Grumman Corporation
company.src: EDGAR submissions JSON, CIK 0001133421 (former name NNG Inc, Feb-Apr 2001)

guidance_fy26.src: Q3 2026 earnings release (Form 8-K Ex. 99, 20-Oct-2026), '2026 Guidance' and '2026 Segment Guidance' tables
guidance_fy26.history: 27-Jan-2026 (Q4-25 release): sales $43,500-44,000m, segment OI $4,850-5,000m, MTM-adjusted EPS $27.40-27.90, FCF $3,100-3,500m; AS mid $13bn / low-to-mid 9%, DS mid-to-high $8bn / ~10%, MS high $12bn / high 14%, SS ~$11bn / ~11%, eliminations ~($2.4bn) / high 13%. 21-Apr-2026: unchanged. 21-Jul-2026: sales raised to $43,750-44,250m, MTM-adjusted EPS to $28.60-29.10, 'free cash flow' relabelled 'adjusted free cash flow' (unchanged $3,100-3,500m); AS ~$14bn / mid-to-high 9%, MS ~15%, SS low 10%, eliminations ~($2.7bn) / mid 13%. 20-Oct-2026: segment OI raised to $4,940-5,040m, MTM-adjusted EPS to $29.35-29.75; AS high 9%, MS mid 15%.
guidance_fy26.not_on_edgar: The company no longer publishes FAS/CAS, unallocated corporate expense, interest, tax-rate or share-count guidance in the release; items of that kind quoted on the earnings call are not verifiable from EDGAR and are not used. Q4/26E point estimates for those lines are derived from the year-to-date run-rate (see the scenario table notes).

share_price.src: Form 4 filed 4-Nov-2026 (Benjamin R. Davies): 281 shares disposed at $555.32 on 2-Nov-2026 (shares withheld); a Form 4 filed 3-Nov-2026 (Mark A. Welsh III) shows open-market sales the same day at $553.39-557.47. Latest share price in an SEC filing; no repurchases in Q3 2026 so the 10-Q carries no average repurchase price. Update to market.

debt.src: FY2025 Form 10-K Note 9 (maturities of long-term debt at 31-Dec-2025) and Q3 2026 Form 10-Q Note 8 / liquidity section
debt.repaid_2026: March 2026: $270m 7.875% notes and $257m 7.75% notes repaid at maturity ($527m; Q3 2026 10-Q)
debt.at_2026_09_30: Long-term debt $14,433m plus current portion $764m = $15,197m (Q3 2026 10-Q); current portion recorded in other current liabilities
debt.issued_2025: May 2025: $500m 4.65% notes due 2030 and $500m 5.25% notes due 2035 ($1.0bn)
debt.facilities: $3.0bn five-year senior unsecured revolving credit facility (2025 Credit Agreement, matures Sep-2030; supports the commercial paper programme), $500m one-year uncommitted facility renewed Apr-2025; no borrowings outstanding at 31-Dec-2025 or 30-Sep-2026
debt.model: Scheduled maturities repaid (2027E $755m, 2028E $2,044m, 2029E $592m, 2030E $1,252m, 2031E: first tranche of 'thereafter', input) and refinanced with new notes at an assumed 5.25% (2025 issue coupons 4.65-5.25%); commercial paper / revolver drawn to a minimum cash balance.

amort_sched.src: FY2025 Form 10-K Note 7: expected future amortization of purchased intangibles; net customer-related and other intangibles $208m at 31-Dec-2025 (gross $3,372m); amortization expense $45m (2025), $57m (2024), $80m (2023)
amort_sched.model: Intangible asset amortization and PP&E step-up depreciation are reported in unallocated corporate expense ($84m in 2025, of which amortization $45m); the model drives the unallocated line directly and shows the schedule as memo.

pension.src: FY2025 Form 10-K Note 12 and MD&A (FAS/CAS operating adjustment table); Q3 2026 release
pension.mtm_sensitivity: FY2025 10-K: +/-100bp of actual vs expected return on plan assets changes 2026 MTM (expense) benefit by about $314m; +/-25bp discount rate about $796m / $(761)m on the obligation
pension.model: FAS/CAS operating adjustment and the non-operating FAS pension benefit are modelled explicitly (non-cash; the pension asset accretes). MTM is nil in the forecast (actuarial gains and losses are not forecast). Contributions held at the 2025-26 run-rate (~$125m p.a., mostly OPB).

buybacks_dividends.src: Q3 2026 Form 10-Q Note 2 and Part II Item 2; XBRL CommonStockDividendsPerShareDeclared
buybacks_dividends.authorization: $2.5bn of the share repurchase authorization remained at 30-Sep-2026 (Dec-2024 programme); no repurchases in Q3 2026; 9M 2026 repurchases $68m (Q1); 2025 $1,168m through 9M / FY2025 per the cash-flow statement

deals.orbital_atk: Acquired 6-Jun-2018 for $7.7bn net of cash acquired plus $1.4bn of debt assumed (Innovation Systems; FY2018 10-K Note 3). Earlier periods as reported.
deals.it_services_divestiture: IT and mission support services business sold to Peraton on 30-Jan-2021 for $3.4bn; pre-tax gain $1,980m in unallocated corporate (expense) income, after-tax ~$1.1bn; divestiture-related unallowable state taxes and transaction costs $(192)m (Q1 2021 release).
deals.training_services_divestiture: Training services business (Defense Systems) sold in Q2 2025: proceeds $333m, pre-tax gain $231m in unallocated corporate expense, $(20)m of unallowable state taxes and transaction costs; 'organic sales' in the 2026 releases exclude $112m of 9M 2025 training services sales (Q3 2026 release).
deals.shipbuilding_spin: Huntington Ingalls Industries spun off 31-Mar-2011; Shipbuilding is in continuing operations in the FY2006-FY2010 columns as originally reported and in discontinued operations from 2011 (FY2011 10-K recast 2010 continuing-operations sales to $28,143m and 2009 to $27,650m: memo rows).
deals.tasc: TASC sold Dec-2009 ($1.65bn); discontinued operations in the FY2009 10-K, which recast 2008 sales to $32,315m (memo).
deals.b21: B-21 LRIP loss provisions: $1,560m pre-tax in Q4 2023 (Aeronautics Systems) and $477m in Q1 2025 (FY2023 / FY2025 10-K).
deals.goodwill_impairment_2008: Q4 2008 goodwill impairment of $3,060m pre-tax (Aerospace $570m, Shipbuilding $2,490m); non-cash, included in operating costs in the FY2008 10-K statement of operations.

realignments: Information & Services (Mission Systems, Information Technology, Technical Services), Aerospace (Integrated Systems, Space Technology), Electronics, Ships (Newport News and Ship Systems merged into Shipbuilding in Jan-2008); Radio Systems to Mission Systems (2007); Electronics businesses to Mission Systems and missile systems to Space Technology (2008)
Aerospace Systems, Electronic Systems, Information Systems, Shipbuilding, Technical Services (FY2009 10-K recast 2008 and 2007)
Aerospace Systems, Mission Systems, Technology Services (2015 and 2014 recast in the FY2016 10-K; 2015 quarters in the 2016 releases)

Aeronautics Systems, Defense Systems, Mission Systems, Space Systems; intangible amortization and PP&E step-up depreciation moved from segment operating income to unallocated corporate expense (2019 and 2018 recast in the FY2020 10-K; 2019 quarters in the 2020 releases)

Programs realigned between Defense Systems and Space Systems (Space Systems 2023 sales $13,946m as reported vs $11,873m recast; Defense Systems $5,862m vs $8,289m); 2023 and 2022 recast in the FY2024 10-K, 2023 quarters in the 2024 releases

Strike and Surveillance Aircraft Solutions (SSAS) from Defense Systems to Aeronautics Systems and related intersegment changes (Defense Systems 2024 sales $8,560m as reported vs $7,399m recast; Aeronautics $12,030m vs $12,396m); 2024 and 2023 recast in the FY2025 10-K, 2024 quarters in the 2025 releases

accounting.asu_2017_07: From Q1 2018 the non-service components of FAS pension cost are presented below operating income ('Non-operating FAS pension benefit'); the FAS/CAS operating adjustment is service-cost-only from 2018 (net total FAS/CAS adjustment through 2017). 2017 comparatives were recast in the 2018 releases (memo keys); 2017 and earlier columns are as originally reported.
accounting.asc_606: Adopted 1-Jan-2018 (full retrospective); 2017 recast sales $26,004m vs $25,803m as reported (memo).
accounting.mtm: Mark-to-market (MTM) pension and OPB accounting adopted in Q4 2018 (actuarial gains and losses recognised in the fourth quarter; 'Mark-to-market pension and OPB (benefit) expense' below operating income). The Q4 2018 release (Schedule 6) recast 2016, 2017 and Q1-Q3 2018: the model's Q1-Q3 2018 columns use that recast (originally reported figures in the cell comments); 2016-17 stay as reported with the recast totals as memo rows. Through 2017 pension cost was recognised with amortization of actuarial gains / losses (no MTM line).
accounting.cash_basis_2018_19: The 2018-2019 cash-flow statements reconcile cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash; the balance sheet shows cash and cash equivalents (difference = restricted cash, memo).

corrections.none: No company figure is overridden. Known data exceptions are documented in the kit README (sparse rows in the FY2006-08 10-K cash-flow statements that cannot be placed are left blank and absorbed in the derived 'other' lines).
